content:
Over the past several days we have been listening carefully to the five different sounds of the two silver trumpets that Yahweh commanded Moses to make in the wilderness. At first they appeared to be simple signals used only to organise the camp of Israel. But as we have studied them more closely, we have discovered that each sound was prophetic. Together they reveal the entire journey of God's people, from the moment they are first called until the day they stand rejoicing in the very presence of Yahweh. Today we come to the fifth and final sound, and it is a fitting place to bring our study to its close, because this fifth sound is the climax of the whole journey.

It is no coincidence that there are five distinct trumpet purposes recorded in Numbers chapter ten. The Law, or Torah, is itself made up of five books; Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy. Just as those five books of Moses reveal Yahweh's plan of redemption from beginning to end, these five trumpet sounds beautifully summarise that same spiritual journey. The Torah was never merely a book of laws and regulations. It was a prophetic testimony, pointing forward to Christ and to the experience of the New Creation. Hidden within these five trumpet blasts is the whole story of our walk with Yahweh.

Let us briefly remember the sounds we have already studied. The first sound gathered the whole congregation before the Tabernacle, reminding us of the Gospel call by which Yahweh gathers His people through his son. The second sound gathered only the leaders, speaking of those whom he calls, teaches, and prepares to shepherd His people and proclaim His truth. The third sound was the alarm that caused the camp to begin its journey through the wilderness, reminding us that our lives are not stationary, but a pilgrimage along the narrow way toward the heavenly Promised Land. The fourth sound was the alarm for battle, teaching us that every disciple of Christ is a soldier engaged in spiritual warfare, fighting the good fight of faith clothed in the whole armour of God. And now we come to the fifth and final sound.

Yahweh said: "Also in the day of your gladness, and in your solemn days, and in the beginnings of your months, ye shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; that they may be to you for a memorial before your God: I am Yahweh your God" (Numbers 10:10). Notice how different this trumpet is from all the others. This is not the trumpet that gathers the people. This is not the trumpet that prepares the leaders. This is not the trumpet that begins the journey. This is not the trumpet that calls soldiers into battle. This is the trumpet of joy. It is sounded during the appointed feasts of Yahweh. It is heard at the New Moon celebrations.
It accompanies the burnt offerings and the peace offerings that are presented before Him. It is the sound of worship, of thanksgiving, of fellowship, and of victory.

Consider the beautiful order in this. After the gathering comes rejoicing. After the journey comes celebration. After the battle comes peace. This is the final destination of every believer. The New Creation is not called merely to fight battles forever. We are not travelling endlessly through the wilderness with no end in sight. Our journey has a glorious destination. Every trumpet that has sounded before this one has been leading us steadily toward this final moment; eternal fellowship with Yahweh. The God who gathered us, prepared us, led us, and fought for us was always bringing us home to Himself, to a place of unbroken joy in His presence.

Let us look at the two offerings over which this trumpet was sounded, because they teach us why our joy is so secure. The burnt offering reminds us of complete dedication and surrender. Under the New Covenant, Christ offered Himself completely to the Father, and because of His perfect sacrifice, we too are able to present ourselves to God. Paul writes: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service" (Romans 12:1). The peace offering speaks of restored fellowship with God. Through the sacrifice of Christ, peace has been made between Yahweh and His people.
As Paul declares: "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ" (Romans 5:1). The trumpet sounded over these offerings because worship is the joyful response of a redeemed people. Israel rejoiced because Yahweh had chosen them to be His own. The New Creation rejoices because Christ has redeemed us and brought us into the household of God.

Throughout the New Testament we are reminded again and again that joy is one of the clear marks of those who belong to Christ. Paul says: "Rejoice in the Lord always: and again I say, Rejoice" (Philippians 4:4). Peter writes that although we have not yet seen Christ with our eyes, we "rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory" (1 Peter 1:8). And so, our lives ends exactly where it began; with worship. We were gathered by worship. We are sustained through worship. And we will enter eternity itself with worship. The trumpet of joy is the sound that surrounds the whole journey of the redeemed, from first to last.

Even today this trumpet of joy is already sounding among God's people.
Every time we gather together to worship Him, every time we celebrate His goodness, every time we remember the sacrifice of Christ at the Lord's Table, every time our hearts overflow with thanksgiving; we hear an echo of this fifth trumpet. It is not only a sound reserved for the future. It is already breaking into our lives now, every time the redeemed lift their hearts to Yahweh in gladness. The feast has not yet fully come, but we are already tasting it.

Yet the greatest fulfilment still lies ahead of us. One day the wilderness journey will be over. The battles will have ended. The armour will no longer be needed. Faith will become sight. The saints will be gathered before His throne. And then the everlasting feast will at last begin. John was given a glimpse of that glorious day when he wrote: "Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God" (Revelation 21:3). That is the final trumpet of joy. No more wandering. No more warfare. No more tears. Only everlasting fellowship with Yahweh, in a joy that will never again be interrupted.

And so, as we conclude this study of the silver trumpets, we can now see the wonderful picture that was hidden within the Law of Moses all along. The five trumpet sounds reveal the entire experience of the New Creation. We are gathered by the Gospel. We are prepared as servants. We journey through the wilderness. We fight the good fight of faith. And at last we enter into everlasting joy and worship in the presence of our God. May we continue to listen carefully for the sound of His trumpet, faithfully following wherever He leads, until the day our pilgrimage ends and our songs of faith become songs of eternal victory before the throne of Yahweh.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,

We thank You that our journey does not end in the battle, but in joy.

You gathered us, prepared us, led us, and fought for us;

and all the while You were bringing us home to Yourself.

Teach us to rejoice even now, in the wilderness, with songs of thanksgiving,

for the trumpet of joy is already echoing among Your redeemed people.

Keep us faithful until the day the feast begins and faith becomes sight,

when there will be no more wandering, no more warfare, and no more tears.

"O give thanks unto Yahweh, for He is good; for His mercy endures forever"

let our every breath be a trumpet of praise to Your name.

In the name of Christ, the Captain of our salvation, we pray. Amen.
